card.band: 20h. Large C codebase; the ceiling needs a rewrite-scale change, so frontier earns partial credit by buckets (small-key GET/SET, hashes, sorted sets, pipelined traffic). Weaker models break replies or persistence.

card.grading: Hidden generated command traces replayed with a client script across data types and sizes. Gate: reply streams and DEBUG DIGEST equal to the reference on all traces, plus a subset of the repo's own tests. Score: median throughput/latency over traces, 2^u-1 against the 9.x speedup.

card.title: Valkey 8.0 to 9.x keyspace and command-path speedup

history: The repo and licence are solid, but the score is a client-server throughput median over loopback under gVisor. gVisor's network stack and syscall overhead would dominate per-command CPU, so the published 17-30% bare-metal gains (no benchmark setup given) likely shrink to near the noise floor. spike_plan.kill_if: 9.1.2 is within 5% of 8.0.x on all families (too little headroom for a reward curve), or run-to-run CV exceeds 10% so the median score is noise.
spike_plan.pass_if: Both builds pass the test subset; reply streams and digests are identical across runs; 9.1.2 beats 8.0.x by at least 15% median on at least one trace family; run-to-run CV is below 5%.
steps: Fetch valkey 8.0.10 and 9.1.2 as source archives (no git history); build both with make in a throwaway container with network.
Run a short runtest subset on both builds to confirm they pass.
Write a trace generator for GET/SET/HSET/ZADD at 16B, 512B and 64KB, pipeline depth 1 and 10, 9 IO threads.
Replay each trace on both builds with redis-benchmark or a custom client; record DEBUG DIGEST and the reply stream for each.
Repeat each run 5 times to measure run-to-run variance of median throughput.
Check that the reply streams and digests match between the two builds for every trace (determinism check).

v1.summary: Valkey 9.1.2 exists and is BSD-3-Clause, so the source and licence claims hold, but the "hashtable rewrite, embedded keys" description is not in the public release notes, which only describe rehash tuning, a string embedding threshold, and an IO-thread redesign. The idea is viable as a 20h optimisation with a history-less snapshot, though the reference's measured speedup on the hidden traces is unknown and must be measured in the spike before the score curve is trusted.

v2.note: The repo and licence are solid, but the score is a client-server throughput median over loopback under gVisor. gVisor's network stack and syscall overhead would dominate per-command CPU, so the published 17-30% bare-metal gains (no benchmark setup given) likely shrink to near the noise floor. IO-thread gains also depend on cgroup CPU behaviour, and cgroup CPU limits are stubs in this sandbox. The hashtable rewrite and embedded keys are not confirmed in the 9.1 notes, the base tag is unpinned, S is unmeasured, and frontier_hours of 30 exceed the 20h tier. The subject also sits next to the crowded Redis-clone family.
